findings.title: Hard-coded utf-8 decode raises UnicodeDecodeError and ignores declared charset
findings.evidence: Body is joined then decoded with a fixed utf-8 codec, ignoring response.encoding/charset and any BOM, and decode errors are not suppressed or wrapped, so a caller that only guards ResponseTooLarge/ValueError gets an unhandled UnicodeDecodeError on any non-UTF-8 body (e.g. text/html in ISO-8859-1).
findings.recommendation: Decode using the response charset (response.encoding or a charset sniff) with an explicit errors policy, and either document or wrap UnicodeDecodeError so the function only raises its documented exceptions.

findings.title: Size-cap logic is untested, including the header-vs-stream paths
findings.evidence: The module ships with no tests for the declared-length rejection, the chunked streaming rejection, the unparsable-header fallthrough, or the exact-boundary (total == max_bytes) case; the behaviour that matters here (a server lying about or omitting Content-Length) is exactly what a regression test would pin down.
findings.evidence_quote: with requests.get(url, timeout=timeout, stream=True) as response:
findings.recommendation: Add tests using a stubbed/mocked Response covering: declared length over cap, declared length absent with a body over cap, body exactly at cap, non-numeric Content-Length, and a non-UTF-8 body.

findings.title: Raising ResponseTooLarge inside a try that catches ValueError is fragile
findings.evidence: The header check raises ResponseTooLarge from inside the same try block whose except clause swallows ValueError; it only survives because ResponseTooLarge currently subclasses Exception, so any future change making it a ValueError subclass (or catching broader exceptions) would silently disable the declared-length guard.
findings.recommendation: Parse the header in the try block and raise ResponseTooLarge after the except, e.g. parse to an int sentinel then compare outside the try, so the guard cannot be swallowed.
